State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Ibibo Group Pvt. Ltd. vs Manish Agarwal & Another on 6 December, 2019
Cause Title/Judgement-Entry STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION WEST BENGAL 11A, Mirza Ghalib Street, Kolkata - 700087   First Appeal No. A/952/2018 ( Date of Filing : 06 Dec 2018 ) (Arisen out of Order Dated 24/09/2018 in Case No. Complaint Case No. CC/374/2017 of District Kolkata-II(Central))   1. IBIBO Group Pvt. Ltd. 2nd Floor, Ideal Plaza, 11/1, Sarat Bose Road, near Minto Park Crossing, W.B., Kolkata - 700 020, P.S. - Shakespeare Sarani. ...........Appellant(s) Versus 1. Manish Agarwal & Another 81/2/7, Phears Lane, Kolkata - 700 012. 2. Interglobe Aviation Ltd. 228-A, A.J.C. Bose Road, 1st Floor, Landmark Building, Kolkata - 700 020, P.S. - Shakespeare Sarani. ...........Respondent(s)   BEFORE:     HON'BLE MR. SAMARESH PRASAD CHOWDHURY PRESIDING MEMBER   HON'BLE MRS. Dipa Sen ( Maity ) MEMBER   For the Appellant: Ms. Suveni Banerjee, Advocate For the Respondent: Ms. Soumi Mukhopadhyay, Advocate Dated : 06 Dec 2019 Final Order / Judgement 

 PER: HON'BLE MR. SAMARESH PRASAD CHOWDHURY, PRESIDING MEMBER
The instant appeal under
Section 15
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') is at the instance of Opposite Party No. 2 IBIBO Group Pvt. Ltd. to impeach the final order/judgment dated 24.09.2018 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Kolkata, Unit-II (in short, 'Ld. District Forum') in Consumer complaint No. 374 of 2017. By the impugned order the Ld. District Forum allowed the complaint lodged by the respondent No. 1 Sri Manish Agarwal  under
Section 12
of the Act with the directions upon the OP No. 2/appellant to refund at Rs. 13,500/-  only being the Air fare, compensation of Rs. 10,000/- and litigation costs of Rs. 5,000/- aggregating Rs. 28,500/- and with a further direction to deposit Rs. 5,000/- as punitive damages for practicing unfair trade practice.
The respondent No. 1 herein being complainant lodged the complaint before the Ld. District Forum stating that he had booked Air Ticket through OP No. 2 from Bangalore to Kolkata for travelling on 05.03.2017 by IndiGo flight No. 6E-529. On arriving at the Bangalore Airport, OP No. 1 informed the complainant that the booking was cancelled. Complainant availed of the same flight by booking another ticket at a higher price in order to see his ailing father at Kolkata. Under compelling circumstances, complainant referred the matter to the Consumer Affairs Department and Fair Business Practices, Government of West Bengal for redressal of his grievances. However, the department could not extend any relief and directed the complainant to approach the appropriate forum under the scheme of the Act. Hence, the respondent No. 1 approached the Ld. District Forum against the IndiGo and also the IBIBO Group through which he purchased the Air Ticket on the allegation of deficiency of services and prayed for refund of the amount of ticket along with compensation and litigation costs etc.

 

          The respondent No. 2 (Opposite Party No. 1) by filing a written version has stated that on 14.02.2017 the booking was cancelled and cancellation fee of Rs. 2250/- was deducted and the remaining amount of Rs. 1193/- was refunded to the account of OP No. 2/appellant. It has also been stated that on the self-same date the complainant booked a fresh ticket from Bangalore to Kolkata in Indigo flight No. 6E-529 under PNR No. BDTUJA and successfully boarded the flight. The OP No. 1 has stated that as there was no deficiency in services from the part of them, the complaint should be dismissed against them.
The appellant being Opposite Party No. 2 did not appear to contest.
After assessing the materials on record, the Ld. District Forum by the impugned order allowed the complaint with certain directions upon the Opposite Party No. 2, as indicated above. To assail the said order OP No. 2 has come up in this commission with the present appeal.
We have considered the submission advanced by Ms. Suveni Banerjee and Ms. Soumi Mukhopadhyay, Ld. Advocate for the appellant and respondent No. 1 respectively. None appears for respondent No. 2 when the record was taken up for hearing of the appeal.
Undisputedly, the respondent No. 1/complainant booked return air tickets for Kolkata/Bangalore sector having departure date of 05.03.2017 from the website of the appellant. The said booking of the respondent No. 1 was issued under the booking ID 116 EFD3BWT. When the respondent No. 1 arrived at Bangalore airport to avail the Indigo Flight being No. 6E-529, he was informed by respondent No. 2/OP No. 1that the booking had been cancelled. It also appears that the respondent No. 1 booked a fresh air ticket from Bangalore to Kolkata on the same flight in order to see his ailing father on payment of charges of Rs. 9696/-.
It may be pertinent to record that the appellant provided the IP address from where the ticket was cancelled and it was appeared to be the portal of appellant. However, the appellant had failed to show any document whatsoever that the said IP address had any nexus with the respondent No. 1 or with respondent No. 2 Indigo Airlines.
From the correspondences it would reveal that the appellant had made a correspondence with the respondent No. 1 on 08.05.2017 at 11.13 AM through e-mail by which the appellant informed respondent No. 1 that they are initiating to refund the air fare. On the self-same date at about 6.39 P.M the appellant company sent another e-mail to respondent No. 1 stating that they will initiate full refund of worth Rs. 3668/- paid by respondent No. 1 in same mode of payment. It may be pertinent to record that the respondent No. 1 purchased the ticket @ Rs. 3668/- and the appellant agreed to refund the same. However, there is no explanation from the side of appellant under what circumstances and in what manner the ticket was cancelled without any information/requisition from the end of respondent No. 1. Due to such negligence on the part of the appellant, respondent No. 1 had to purchase the ticket of the same flight at a costs of Rs. 9696/-. Further, it causes undue harassment and mental agony to the respondent No. 1.
In that perspective, the Ld. District Forum has rightly allowed the complaint when there is apparent negligence or deficiency in rendering services by the appellant to respondent No.1.
However, the Ld. District Forum had no reason to direct the OP No. 2/appellant to refund Rs. 13,500/- only being air ticket fare, more particularly, when the respondent No. 1 purchased the ticket at a price of 9696/-. Therefore, the Ld. District Forum should have directed OP No. 2/appellant to refund Rs. 9696/- being the price of air ticket fare to avail the flight. Considering  the loss suffered by the appellant, we think a compensation of Rs. 10,000/- is on the higher side and considering the fact that the respondent No. 1 could avail the same flight which he intended to board, we think instead of  Rs. 10,000/- a compensation of Rs. 2,000/- in the facts and circumstances will meet the ends of justice. Considering the expenses incurred by the respondent No. 1 for the litigation, we think instead of Rs. 5,000/-, the Ld. District Forum should have awarded litigation cost at Rs. 3,000/-.
The Ld. District Forum has imposed punitive damages of Rs. 5,000/-. The Ld. District Forum had no reason to impose punitive damages, when there was no averment in the petition of complaint or any prayer in the prayer clause of the petition of complaint to that effect. In a decision reported in (2015) 1 SCC 429 [General Motors (India) Private Limited -vs- Ashok Ramlal Tolat and Anr.) the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed- "normally punitive damages are awarded against a conscious wrong doing unrelated to the actual loss suffered. Such a claim has to be specifically pleaded."
In the facts and circumstances of the present case, we do not find any such averment with regard to conscious wrong doing on the part of appellant. Considering the above, the order imposed as punitive damages is liable to be set aside.
In view of the above, the impugned judgment/final order is modified to the extent that the appellant/Opposite Party No. 2 shall refund Rs. 9696/- being the air ticket fare, Rs. 2,000/- as compensation and Rs. 3,000/- as litigation cost aggregating Rs. 14,696/- to be paid  within 45 days from date, in default the amount shall carry interest @ 9% p.a. from date till its realisation.
With the above observations and directions, the instant appeal stands disposed of.
The Registrar Commission is directed to send a copy of the order to the LD. District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Kolkata, Unit-II for information.
